description: Compare one number across a handful of categories, e.g. sales by country, count per product.
One or a few numbers changing over time, e.g. monthly revenue, yearly GDP, daily users.
How a total over time splits into parts, e.g. energy mix per year, traffic by source per month.
Composition or breakdown of each category into parts or shares, e.g. budget by department and cost type, survey answers per group.
Relationship between two numeric variables across many items, e.g. price vs rating, GDP vs life expectancy, correlation.
Distribution of one numeric variable, e.g. spread of salaries, ages, response times, how values are distributed.
A value for every combination of two categories or a grid, e.g. activity by weekday and hour, matrix of countries by sector.
Share of a whole across many items or a hierarchy, e.g. market share, budget split, portfolio composition.
Share of a whole across very few parts (2 to 5), e.g. percent yes/no, gender split.
Flows from sources to destinations, e.g. migration between regions, funnel of users between steps, money flowing from A to B.
Rankings changing over time, e.g. league table positions per season, top models by rank each month.
Before vs after or two values per category, gaps, e.g. 2020 vs 2025 per country, men vs women pay gap.
